findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator applies numeric math to the `datetime` key, so the optimized path crashes.
findings.body: The endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `self.key` is `datetime`. `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on a `datetime` object, which raises `TypeError`. `build_cursor` calls `get_item_key` on every page that has results, so every optimized request with any audit entries returns a 500. `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw numeric cursor value, and `build_queryset` then compares it against a DateTimeField. DateTimePaginator converts epoch milliseconds to a datetime first, and this one does not. Fix: subclass DateTimePaginator, or copy its key and cursor conversion.

findings.title: Negative offsets from the client are passed straight into a Django queryset slice, which raises an error.
findings.body: `cursor.offset` comes from the client's `cursor` query parameter. If a caller sends a cursor such as `0:-10:0`, this branch runs `queryset[-10:...]`. Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise `ValueError`/`AssertionError`, so the request fails with a 500 instead of returning a page. The comments say "the ORM properly handles negative slicing" and that this "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds", and both are wrong. Fix: remove the branch and clamp the offset with `max(0, offset)` in every case.

findings.title: The admin check is wrong, and it runs on every request even when the optimized path is not requested.
findings.body: `request.user.is_superuser` is true for a superuser account even without an active superuser session. Sentry normally checks `is_active_superuser(request)`. `member.has_global_access` is also true for every member of an open-membership org, so the check does not limit this to administrators. The line runs before `use_optimized` is checked, so when `organization_context.member` is None (for example a staff or token request without a membership), it raises `AttributeError` and breaks the normal audit-log listing too. I could not check whether `member` can be None at this point. Fix: evaluate the check only when `use_optimized` is set, use `is_active_superuser(request)`, and guard against `member` being None.
